messages:
elaine: FYI ran a regional CP split test this morning. During peering preemption some tenants saw outbound IP flips and short TCP stalls. not a full outage but enough noise.
tom: saw the traces. interestingly, the flip often happened when the new regional connector announced route before old connector finished NAT teardown. conntrack was gone.
rafa: this is similar to connector eviction issues but the root cause here is the CP split ordering + ephemeral ip-pool sizing. we exhausted ephemeral pool then reassigned IPs aggressively.
elaine: quick brainstorm: instead of relying only on lease TTL, what about issuing short-lived affinity tokens for long-lived flows. token binds tenant -> src_ip and can be used by routing fabric to prefer the old SNAT for that tuple for N seconds.
tom: affinity-token sounds promising. how would it be carried? add to dataplane headers? store in a lightweight distributed affinity cache?
rafa: implementation sketch: agent mints token when conntrack sees L4 session > threshold. token short (eg 120s). routing layer has an affinity cache keyed by (tenant, token) mapping to connector ENI. new connector advertising route checks cache and optionally DNAT-bounces to old ENI while old connector drains.
elaine: DNAT-bounce = novel: rather than rewriting source at the new connector (which would change IP), the new connector rewrites destination to route through the old ENI path so original src preserved. effectively a temporary DNAT to preserve client-facing IP.
tom: downside: extra hop and latency for flows in bounce window. we'd have to measure CPU and pps cost. also TLS SNI/logging may show intermediate hop which confuses some customers.
rafa: tradeoffs:
- affinity-token + affinity-cache: extra distributed state but minimal per-packet work (single lookup)
- DNAT-bounce: heavier but avoids global state if we implement token as simple sticky hint in routing table
- lease-extension: simpler but ties up ENIs longer

elaine: lean proposal: combine all three but with conservative defaults: tokens for L4 > 30s, token_ttl=120s, DNAT-bounce enabled only for tenants that opt-in or flagged by SLA, lease_extension short (30s), soft-drain 60s.
rafa: example config (pseudo):
```
egress_affinity:
  token_threshold_s: 30
  token_ttl_s: 120
  default_soft_drain_s: 60
  dnbackoff_enabled: false  # DNAT-bounce off by default
  dnbackoff_opt_in_label: "stable-egress"
ephemeral_pool:
  max_ephemeral_per_az: 50
  reserve_ratio: 0.1
```
tom: ops notes: need to ensure affinity cache has bounded size + LRU eviction; also fallback behavior when cache miss: proceed with normal connector assignment, maybe increment snat_fallback metric.
ops-bot: recommended metrics to add: egress_affinity_tokens_issued_total, egress_affinity_cache_misses, dnbackoff_invocations_total, tenant_stable_optins_total.
rafa: also add alert if ephemeral_pool_usage > 85% for any AZ. that's the leading indicator for aggressive reassigns.
elaine: customer-facing: provide stable-egress opt-in flag per tenant; document latency tradeoff for DNAT-bounce. probably paid tier given IP cost.
tom: testing plan: canary in us-west with 5 tenants, enable tokens, DNAT off. run long-lived tcp uploads and trigger peering failover. measure tenant_ip_flip_count and p95 latency.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job: egress-affinity-canary at 2026-04-10T01:00Z, owners: @rafa @elaine.
rafa: i'll land a small spike PR that implements token mint + cache read path in routing fabric and a canary dashboard.
elaine: add runbook steps: how to force-clear affinity cache, how to disable DNAT-bounce globally, and how to revert token issuance if cache overload.
tom: one more: consider per-tenant sticky-route TTL so external BGP/peers see consistent egress for at least token_ttl_s. might help whitelisting customers. ops-bot: note added.
elaine: thanks all, this preserves connection continuity without holding ENIs forever. we'll iterate after canary results.
